title: Prompt quality and layout (cache and answer quality together)

questions.text: Which held-out cases (never used while writing the prompt) and which metric decide that this prompt change is better, and what are the baseline numbers before the change?

Write the request in render order: tools, system (role, stable instructions, examples), long documents, then the question and anything that varies per call. Where is each breakpoint, and does anything that changes per call or per user sit before one?
For inputs over ~20k tokens: are the documents above the question and instructions, each in <document> with <source> and <document_content>, and does the prompt ask for the relevant quotes first?

Are there 3-5 examples that are relevant, diverse and wrapped in <example> tags? Are they one fixed set inside the stable prefix, or picked per call (then after the breakpoint, in a deterministic order)? Do they replace a list of edge-case rules?
Are tag names and their order the same on every call, with the varying content only inside tags after the breakpoint? Is any object serialised into the prompt with a stable key order?
Does the model need the date or time? Where does it go (after the last breakpoint), at which granularity (the day, not the millisecond), and in which time zone?

Does any request end with an assistant turn (prefill)? Which model runs it (prefill is rejected with a 400 from Claude 4.6 on), and what replaces it: structured outputs, a tool with an enum, or a plain instruction?

If the prompt is reordered or split for caching: which quality A/B runs before and after on the held-out cases (same model, parameters and cases), and which cache numbers (cache-probe.mjs) show the gain?
How many tools and how many tokens of tool definitions does each request load? At 10+ tools or 10k+ tokens, why not tool search with defer_loading (keeping the 3-5 most used loaded)?

If an LLM grades the output: is there a written rubric per dimension, one isolated judge per dimension, an 'Unknown' way out, thinking on, and an agreement number against human labels on a labelled sample? Do the cases test both when the behaviour should and should not happen?

If history is compacted or summarised: was the summary prompt tuned on real long traces (recall first, then precision), are the recent turns kept word for word, and is there a breakpoint at the end of the system prompt so compaction only writes the summary?

budgets.measure: cases in the held-out set used for the before/after decision (prompt-ab.mjs n)
budgets.source: Anthropic, Define success criteria and build evaluations: a held-out test set, more automated cases over fewer hand-graded ones (the count is a judgement threshold)

budgets.measure: paired difference after - before on the held-out cases: the lower end of its 95% interval must stay above -2 points (prompt-ab.mjs verdict)
budgets.source: judgement threshold; non-inferiority on a held-out set

budgets.measure: agreement between the judge and human labels on a labelled sample (prompt-ab.mjs judge: agreement and Cohen's kappa)
budgets.source: Anthropic, Demystifying evals for AI agents: LLM-as-judge graders closely calibrated with human experts (the number is a judgement threshold)

budgets.measure: count_tokens of the document part; above it, documents go before the question
budgets.source: Anthropic prompting best practices: long context prompting (20k+ tokens), queries at the end up to 30% better

budgets.measure: examples in <example> tags for a format- or tone-sensitive task (3-5)
budgets.source: Anthropic prompting best practices: include 3-5 examples

budgets.measure: count_tokens of the tool definitions loaded up front; above it (or at 10+ tools), defer with tool search
budgets.source: Anthropic tool search tool: use it at 10+ tools or 10k+ tokens of definitions

rules.title: Question interpolated before the documents in one prompt template
rules.why: Long documents answer better with the question at the end (up to 30% in Anthropic's tests), and the documents are the part that repeats, so they belong before the varying question for the cache too.
rules.confirm: measurement: prompt-ab.mjs on held-out cases with the documents moved above the question; plus cache-probe.mjs replay of two questions on the same documents
rules.fixHint: documents first in <documents><document index><source><document_content>, then the instructions and the question

rules.title: Request ends with a literal assistant turn (prefill)
rules.why: From Claude 4.6 on, a prefilled last assistant turn is rejected with a 400; the call works on an old model and breaks on the upgrade.
rules.confirm: failing-test: send the request to a current model (or a recorded 400) and assert it fails; static-proof: the assistant literal is the last message
rules.fixHint: structured outputs or a tool with an enum for formats and labels; an instruction for preambles

rules.title: Few-shot examples shuffled or sampled per call
rules.why: Examples sit early in the prompt: a new order or subset per call moves the cached prefix, and the output varies with the draw, so a before/after comparison measures noise.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache-probe.mjs replay of the same input twice (prefix-moved); prompt-ab.mjs of the same prompt against itself across seeds shows the spread
rules.fixHint: one fixed, curated set in the stable prefix; if examples must be picked per input, pick them deterministically and place them after the breakpoint

rules.title: Tag names, section order or serialised key order that change between calls
rules.why: The model reads a moving layout, and every variant is a new cached prefix.
rules.confirm: measurement: render the prompt for two inputs and diff up to the breakpoint; cache-probe.mjs replay verdict prefix-moved

rules.title: Prompt reordered or split for caching with no quality comparison
rules.why: A layout that caches better can answer worse (an instruction moved away from what it governs, documents moved after the question); the cost win hides a quality loss.
rules.confirm: measurement: prompt-ab.mjs on held-out cases before vs after the reorder; verdict regressed

rules.title: A growing list of edge-case rules in the prompt instead of examples
rules.why: Each case gets a rule, the rules collide, and the prompt gets longer and more brittle; a few canonical examples carry the behaviour better.
rules.confirm: measurement: prompt-ab.mjs with the rule list replaced by 3-5 canonical examples

rules.title: LLM judge with no agreement number against human labels, or one judge grading every dimension
rules.why: An uncalibrated judge can reward the wrong thing; every decision taken on its scores inherits the error.
rules.confirm: measurement: prompt-ab.mjs judge on a labelled sample: agreement under prompt.judge_human_agreement_min

rules.title: Eval cases only where the behaviour should happen (or only where it should not)
rules.why: One-sided cases optimise one side: an agent tested only on when to search learns to search for everything.
rules.confirm: static-proof: the case list has no negative (or no positive) cases for the behaviour

rules.title: Dozens of tools or 10k+ tokens of tool definitions loaded on every request
rules.why: Tool choice gets worse past 30-50 tools and every request pays for definitions it does not use.
rules.confirm: measurement: count_tokens of the tools array; tool-selection accuracy on held-out cases with and without tool search

rules.title: Compaction or summary prompt never tuned on real long traces
rules.why: Aggressive compaction drops context whose importance shows only later; the agent then repeats work or contradicts itself.
rules.confirm: measurement: replay long real traces through the compactor and check that later turns still find each fact they used (recall of facts used after the cut)

verify.text: before/after on the held-out cases with the same model, parameters and cases: prompt-ab.mjs verdict ok (n >= prompt.heldout_cases_min, lower bound of the paired difference above -prompt.quality_drop_max_pp)
after a reorder for cache: cache-probe.mjs replay verdict ok on two different inputs sharing the prefix, and cache-probe.mjs usage hit_pct up on the site
judge calibration: agreement and kappa against human labels on a labelled sample, at or above prompt.judge_human_agreement_min, before its scores decide anything
render the prompt for two different inputs: identical bytes up to the last breakpoint (tags, order, examples, keys)
verify.tool: unit test on the prompt builder

verify.text: scan clean for prompt.question-before-docs, prompt.prefill-last-turn, prompt.shuffled-examples on the diff

tactics.tactic: Long documents at the top in <documents><document index="n"><source>...<document_content>, instructions and the question after them
tactics.when: inputs over ~20k tokens, or any repeated document asked several questions
tactics.saving: up to 30% better answers in Anthropic's tests, and the documents become a cacheable prefix

tactics.tactic: Ask for the relevant quotes first (in <quotes>), then the answer from them
tactics.when: long-document tasks where the answer depends on a few passages
tactics.saving: focus on the relevant content; the quotes make the answer checkable

tactics.tactic: 3-5 relevant, diverse examples in <example> tags (several inside <examples>), one fixed set in the stable prefix
tactics.when: output format, tone or structure matters
tactics.saving: more accurate and consistent output; a fixed set stays cached

tactics.tactic: Replace the edge-case rule list with a few diverse, canonical examples
tactics.when: the prompt grows one rule per bug

tactics.tactic: Consistent, descriptive tag names in the same order on every call; varying content only inside tags after the breakpoint; nested tags for hierarchy; stable key order when serialising
tactics.saving: unambiguous parsing and one cached prefix

tactics.tactic: Say why an instruction matters instead of shouting it (NEVER, ALL CAPS)
tactics.saving: the model generalises from the reason

tactics.tactic: Replace a last-turn prefill with structured outputs, a tool with an enum for labels, or a plain instruction for preambles
tactics.when: a request ending with an assistant turn
tactics.saving: keeps working on Claude 4.6 and later, which return 400 on prefill

tactics.tactic: Tool search with defer_loading: true on rarely used tools, the 3-5 most used kept loaded, a breakpoint on a non-deferred tool
tactics.when: 10+ tools, 10k+ tokens of definitions, or several MCP servers
tactics.saving: over 85% fewer definition tokens in Anthropic's example; selection accuracy holds past 30-50 tools; the cached prefix is untouched when tools load

tactics.tactic: Tune the compaction prompt on real long traces: maximise recall first, then cut superfluous content; keep recent turns word for word; prefer server-side compaction
tactics.when: a loop or chat that summarises its history
tactics.saving: long tasks keep their facts after the cut

tactics.tactic: Before and after any prompt change or reorder: same held-out cases, model and parameters; paired comparison with an interval; ship only when it excludes a drop larger than the budget, then confirm the cache gain with cache-probe
tactics.when: any prompt change, especially a reorder for caching
tactics.saving: no silent quality regression bought with a cost win

tactics.tactic: Judge with a written rubric per dimension, one isolated judge per dimension, an 'Unknown' way out and thinking on; measure agreement with human labels before trusting it
tactics.saving: decisions taken on scores that match expert judgement

tactics.tactic: Test both the cases where the behaviour should happen and where it should not
tactics.when: an eval for a behaviour (search, tool call, refusal, asking back)

tactics.tactic: Load the smallest set of high-signal tokens: identifiers and just-in-time retrieval through tools instead of everything up front
tactics.when: a context that grows with retrieved or tool output
tactics.saving: accuracy and recall degrade as context grows (context rot)
